column1: # Action script: lock/unlock and scroll.
# One prompt per line. Do the step, then press ENTER -- steps are not timed, so
# take as long as you need (entering a passcode, waiting for an animation).
# Lines starting with "!" are setup: not traced, not recorded as a window.
# Step 1 is a liveness check, not data. Moving the pointer over the phone view
# is known to make Device Hub send AbsolutePointer reports. If that window comes
# back empty, the taps did not bind and every negative result in the run is
# void.
# Steps 5 and 6 are the pointer-precedence test: the same scroll gesture with
# and without an established pointer position. If scroll only works after the
# pointer has been moved onto the view, that is the answer to why ipb's
# ScrollReport is accepted and ignored.
! Unlock the phone (type the passcode if it asks) and leave it on the Home screen
! Bring Device Hub to the front, with the phone screen visible
LIVENESS: move the mouse slowly back and forth over the phone view, then stop
Do nothing at all (idle baseline)
Press Command-L to LOCK the screen
! Unlock the phone again -- type the passcode if it asks. Take your time.
Open Settings on the phone and scroll it to somewhere in the middle of a long list
Move the mouse ONTO the phone view and leave it resting over the list, without clicking
Two-finger scroll DOWN on the trackpad, twice, without moving the pointer off the list
Move the mouse well OUTSIDE the phone view, then two-finger scroll DOWN twice
Do nothing at all (idle baseline)
